question: Where are MOST of the world's lakes?

post.premise: One country holds more lakes than the rest of the planet
post.bait: It is not Finland, the land of a thousand lakes.
post.sources_line: Messager et al. 2016 (HydroLAKES, Nature Communications); Natural Resources Canada; Britannica

youtube.title: Most lakes in the world — where are they? Not Finland 🛶
youtube.description:
Russia, Finland or the third one? One country holds more lakes than every other nation on Earth combined, and the reason is a vanished sheet of ice.
Guess before the map fills, then watch the bars grow, see the ice-age why, and take a canoe ride between two giant northern lakes.
Which one did you pick? Tell us below.

instagram.caption:
Where are MOST of the world's lakes? 🛶
Russia, Finland or the other one? One nation holds more than every other country combined, close to 900,000 of them, and the reason is a vanished sheet of ice.
Which did you pick?

facebook.text:
Where are most of the world's lakes — Russia, Finland or Canada?
One of them holds more lakes than the rest of the world combined. How many of them have you actually swum in?

twitter.text:
Where are MOST of the world's lakes?
One nation holds more lakes than the rest of the planet combined. Not Finland.

threads.text: Where are most of the world's lakes — Russia, Finland or Canada? One of them holds more lakes than the rest of the world combined, thanks to an ice sheet that scraped the land bare, and two of its giants sit where almost nobody lives.

intent: The land-of-a-thousand-lakes misdirect: Finland is the famous one, Russia the big one, but Canada holds more lakes than the rest of the world combined — shown as bars, explained by ice, and felt with a canoe ride between two giant northern lakes.

v04.text: Canada. Count every lake you could sail on, and Canada holds more than the rest of the world combined.

v05.text: Nearly 880,000 lakes. Russia, in second, has about 200,000. Finland is not close.

v06.text: Why? Ice. The last ice age scraped the land bare, and the meltwater filled every hollow it left.

v07.text: Great Bear and Great Slave, far north, are giants, and most Canadians have never seen them.

v08.text: More lakes than you thought. Follow us.

research.topic: Country with the most lakes: Canada — ≈ 879,800 lakes above 0.1 sq km (HydroLAKES, Messager et al. 2016), about 62 % of the world's 1.42 million lakes of that size; Russia ≈ 201,200 second, USA ≈ 102,500; cause: Pleistocene glaciation; Great Bear (8th greatest) and Great Slave (10th greatest, deepest in North America) in the Northwest Territories

myths.myth: Finland, the land of a thousand lakes, has the most lakes.
myths.reality: Finland has ~188,000 lakes of all sizes but Canada has about 880,000 lakes above the sailing-size threshold — more than every other country combined by that count.

landscape.our_gap: Lake Shorts are 'top 10 greatest lakes' lists; nobody asks the count as a question, shows the bars, explains the ice, and rides between two lakes almost nobody has seen.

hydrolakes.title: Messager et al. 2016 — Estimating the volume and age of water stored in global lakes using a geo-statistical approach (HydroLAKES)
hydrolakes.notes: 1.42 million lakes above 0.1 sq km worldwide; Canada ≈ 879,800 (≈ 62 %), Russia ≈ 201,200, USA ≈ 102,500

nrcan_lakes.title: Canada's lakes and freshwater
nrcan_lakes.notes: Canada has more lake surface than any other country; nearly 9 % of its territory is fresh water; Great Bear and Great Slave are its two greatest lakes

wiki_lakes.notes: HydroLAKES counts: Canada 879,800; Russia 201,200; USA 102,500; Finland ~56,000 above 0.1 sq km

britannica_gbl.title: Great Bear Lake / Great Slave Lake
britannica_gbl.notes: Great Bear Lake 31,328 sq km, greatest entirely within Canada; Great Slave Lake 28,568 sq km, deepest in North America (614 m); both in the Northwest Territories

usgs_glaciation.title: Glaciers and glacial landforms — origin of lake basins
usgs_glaciation.notes: the Laurentide ice sheet covered nearly all of Canada; glacial scour and moraine damming created most of the lakes of the Canadian Shield
